title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered to me.
body:
It felt like the news landscape was broken. We were either bombarded with sensational headlines meant to trigger a reaction or buried under an endless stream of noise that felt disconnected from my life. I wanted something that respected my time and my intelligence.

Building Headlinne wasn't about trying to disrupt the industry or chasing the latest hype cycle. It was about solving a personal problem. I wanted a way to filter out the noise and find the signal. I wanted technology that worked for me, not against my attention span.

We built this using AI, not because AI is popular, but because it is the only way to genuinely personalize the experience at scale. It allows us to learn what you care about and deliver news that actually fits your interests. It is about making information useful again rather than just abundant.

The journey has taught me that the best products often come from the simplest frustrations. We are still learning and iterating every single day, but the goal remains the same: to make staying informed feel like a privilege instead of a chore.
cta: If you are ready to rethink how you consume your daily news, you can try it yourself at HEADLINNE.com.
